title: Generating text
objectives: Build a sampler with temperature and top-k for the tiny GPT.

screens.title: Always the likeliest
screens.prose: The model has read `My lord, I wi`. One way to write text is to take the likeliest next character every time, then read again.
screens.question: Starting from `First Citizen:` and a new line, the likeliest-first rule writes 60 characters. What do you expect?

options.text: One short phrase, repeated
A fresh line of the play each time
options.why: The rule always takes the same choice from the same context, and short loops are likely contexts.

options.text: It stops after the first word
options.why: Nothing stops it: it writes until 60 characters are done.

options.text: Random characters, as in noise
options.why: Nothing is random: the likeliest character is fixed by the context.

hints.text: Once a phrase repeats, the context the model reads repeats too.
Then the likeliest next character repeats.
Look for a loop.

feedback.correct: It writes `The the the the the the the th`... and loops: the same context gives the same choice.
feedback.generic: Not quite. What happens once a context comes round again?

explain.text: Taking the top character gave `The the the the the the the the the the the t`. **Greedy decoding** often falls into loops, because a repeated context gives a repeated choice.

screens.title: Temperature
screens.prose: Sampling draws the next character at random with the model's chances. Dividing the logits by a **temperature** $\tau$ before the softmax reshapes them. Slide $\tau$ for the model after `My lord, I wi`.
screens.question: What is the chance of `l` at $\tau = 2$? Give 3 decimal places.

hints.text: Slide to the last frame.
Read the `l` bar.

feedback.correct: At $\tau = 2$ the chance of `l` drops from 0.619 to 0.316; the others gain.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Read the `l` bar at $\tau = 2$.

byKey.t05: That is $\tau = 0.5$, which sharpens. Slide to 2.

explain.text: Above 1, $\tau$ flattens the chances: `l` falls to 0.316. Below 1 it sharpens them, and `l` rises to 0.834 at $\tau = 0.5$.

screens.title: Temperature by hand
screens.prose: Three characters have logits 2, 1 and 0. With temperature $\tau$ the chances are $p_i = e^{z_i/\tau} / \sum_j e^{z_j/\tau}$.
screens.question: What is the chance of `a` at $\tau = 0.5$? Give 4 decimal places.

hints.text: Divide each logit by 0.5.
The logits become 4, 2 and 0.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide the logits by $\tau$, then take the softmax.

byKey.tau1: That is $\tau = 1$. Divide the logits by 0.5 first.
byKey.times: You multiplied by 0.5, which flattens. Divide by $\tau$.

explain.text: Halving $\tau$ doubles the gaps between logits: (4, 2, 0) gives `a` 0.8668, up from 0.6652. Low temperature sharpens, high temperature flattens.

screens.title: Keep the top k
screens.prose: **Top-$k$ sampling** keeps the $k$ largest logits, sets the rest to $-\infty$, then takes the softmax. Rare characters can then never be drawn.
screens.question: At $\tau = 1$ and $k = 2$, what is the chance of `a`? Give 4 decimal places.

hints.text: Drop `c`, then softmax over `a` and `b`.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Take the softmax over the kept logits only.

byKey.no-renorm: That is the chance before cutting. Without `c` the two kept chances must add to 1.
byKey.third: You gave each kept character an equal share. The softmax keeps their ratio.

explain.text: Cutting `c` and taking the softmax again gives `a` 0.7311 and `b` 0.2689. The ratio $e^{2-1} = e$ between them is unchanged.

screens.question: Write `sample_next`.

hints.text: Handle temperature 0 first, before any division.
For top-$k$: the $k$-th largest is `np.sort(z)[-k]`; set smaller logits to `-np.inf`.
Softmax: subtract the largest, exponentiate, divide by the sum.

feedback.correct: Your draws match the seeded reference at every temperature.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Check the first failing test.

byKey.test-1: Test 1 uses temperature 0. Return the argmax without dividing.
byKey.test-2: Test 2 draws at $\tau = 1$. Check the softmax and the call `rng.choice(len(z), p=p)`.
byKey.test-7: Test 7: a greedy step must not touch `rng`, so later draws stay the same.

explain.text: With the same generator, the same logits give the same draws, so the tests compare exactly. $k = 1$ keeps only the largest logit: top-1 is greedy decoding.

screens.title: Temperature zero
screens.prose: A colleague's sampler computes `softmax(logits / temperature)` for every temperature. A user sets the temperature to 0 to get the most likely text.
screens.question: What should temperature 0 do?

options.text: Take the largest logit: the limit of ever smaller $\tau$
Raise an error, since $\tau = 0$ means nothing
options.why: As $\tau$ falls the largest logit takes all the chance. $\tau = 0$ is that limit, greedy decoding, and users rely on it.

options.text: Give every character the same chance
options.why: That is the limit of a very large $\tau$, the other end.

options.text: The same as $\tau = 1$
options.why: Lower $\tau$ sharpens; it does not leave the chances alone.

hints.text: Watch the gaps grow as $\tau$ falls.
At $\tau = 0.1$ the top logit is 10 ahead.
The limit puts all the chance on the largest.

feedback.correct: Dividing by 0 gives infinities and `nan`; the meaning of $\tau \to 0$ is greedy, so handle it as argmax.
feedback.generic: Not quite. What happens to the chances as $\tau$ shrinks?

byKey.crash: That is the bug: dividing by 0. Users who ask for $\tau = 0$ want the greedy choice.

explain.text: As $\tau \to 0$ the largest logit wins every draw. So code temperature 0 as argmax rather than dividing by 0.

Return the whole text. `forward`, `sample_next`, `encode`, `decode` and `W` are defined.

screens.title: The window slides
screens.prose: The context is 32 characters. Once the text is longer, each prediction reads only its last 32 characters.

state.caption: The window after 47 characters: indices 15 to 46.

screens.question: A 7-character prompt has grown by 40 generated characters. Numbering from 0, what is the index of the oldest character the next prediction reads?

hints.text: The text now has 47 characters, indices 0 to 46.
The window is the last 32.

feedback.correct: 47 characters, last 32 of them: indices 15 to 46.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Take the last 32 of 47 characters.

byKey.off: You started one too late: the window holds 32 characters, 15 to 46.
byKey.prompt: The prompt has slid out of the window.

explain.text: With 47 characters, the window is indices 15 to 46. The model forgets everything before it, which is one reason long generated text drifts.

screens.question: What has this model of 18,017 parameters learned?

options.text: The look of the text: names, line breaks, word shapes
Sentences that make sense as English
options.why: Most words are not English and no sentence carries meaning.

options.text: To copy out the training text
options.why: The sample is not in the training text; it is drawn character by character.

options.text: Nothing beyond chance, like noise
options.why: Its loss is far below $\ln 65$, and the sample has the shape of a play.

hints.text: Look at the lines that end in a colon.
Look at the lengths of the words.
Then try to read a sentence.

feedback.correct: It writes Shakespeare-shaped nonsense: the format and the spelling patterns, not the meaning.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Read the sample closely.

screens.title: Decoding choices
screens.prose:
Every sampler is one loop with one choice inside it:
```python
for _ in range(n):
    z = forward(W, ids[-T:])[-1] / tau
    z = top_k(z, k)       # optional
    ids.append(draw(softmax(z)))
```
$\tau = 0$ and $k = 1$ both give greedy decoding.
screens.question: Which setting makes two runs from the same prompt give different text?

options.text: $\tau = 1$ with a new seed each run

options.why: Greedy decoding draws nothing, so every run is the same.

options.text: $k = 1$ at any $\tau$
options.why: One kept character has chance 1: greedy again.

options.text: $\tau = 1$ with the same seed
options.why: The same seed gives the same draws, so the same text.

hints.text: Which settings involve a random draw?

feedback.correct: Only a real draw with a fresh seed varies the text.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the setting with a draw whose randomness changes.

explain.text: Text varies only through the draws. Fix the seed, or decode greedily, and the output repeats exactly.

screens.title: Summaries that change
screens.prose: An analyst asks a language model to summarise the same earnings call twice and gets two different summaries. The compliance team wants every published summary reproducible.
screens.question: What should the team record or set?

options.text: Model, prompt, decoding settings and seed
Only the prompt they typed
options.why: The same prompt gives different draws at $\tau > 0$ unless the seed is fixed too.

options.text: A higher temperature, so summaries agree
options.why: A higher temperature makes runs differ more.

options.text: Only the model version they used
options.why: The same model samples differently on every run with a fresh seed.

hints.text: List everything the sampled text depends on.
Weights, prompt, decoding settings, random draws.
Fix or record each.

feedback.correct: A summary is a draw: fix or record everything it depends on, including the seed.
feedback.generic: Not quite. What changes between the two runs?

explain.text: The text depends on the weights, the prompt, $\tau$, $k$ and the draws. Record all of them, or decode at temperature 0, and a summary can be reproduced. Hosted services may still vary slightly from run to run.

ideas: Generation reads the last 32 characters, samples one from the last position's chances, appends it and repeats.
Temperature divides the logits: below 1 sharpens, above 1 flattens; $\tau = 0$ is greedy, coded as argmax. Top-$k$ keeps the $k$ largest; $k = 1$ is greedy.
One seeded generator makes a run repeatable; greedy decoding loops on small models.

quiz.question: Why does greedy decoding of a small model often repeat a phrase forever?

options.text: Once a phrase repeats, the window repeats, so the choice repeats
Its context is too short to store the phrase
options.why: The loop needs only the last few characters to come round again.

options.text: Its random generator repeats
options.why: Greedy decoding uses no random numbers.

feedback.correct: The same context gives the same top character, so a loop feeds itself.
feedback.generic: Not quite. What decides the next character when nothing is random?

explain.text: Greedy decoding is a function of the window. When the window comes round again, so does everything after it.
